title.description: A title for these release notes, e.g. 'v1.3.0' or 'Changes since v1.2.0'.

range.description: The commit range these notes cover, e.g. 'v1.2.0..v1.3.0' or 'main..HEAD'.

summary.description: A 1-3 sentence highlight of the most important changes in this range, in changelog voice. State plainly when there are no user-facing changes.

features.description: New capabilities or user-facing additions. Empty if none.

description.description: A user-facing, one-line description of the addition -- rewritten for a reader, not the raw commit subject.

commits.description: Short hashes of the commits this entry covers (optional).

description.description: A user-facing, one-line description of the fix -- what was broken and is now fixed.

commits.description: Short hashes of the commits this entry covers (optional).

breaking_changes.description: Backward-incompatible changes -- a changed function signature or API shape, a removed/renamed CLI flag or config key, a changed default, or an altered on-disk/wire format. Anything that forces a user to adapt. Empty if none.

description.description: What changed and why it breaks backward compatibility.

migration.description: The concrete step a user must take to adapt (e.g. 'rename the `db_path` config key to `database.path`').

commits.description: Short hashes of the commits this entry covers (optional).

other.description: Notable internal changes worth mentioning (performance, refactors, docs, tooling) that are not features or fixes. Empty if none.

description.description: A one-line description of the change.

commits.description: Short hashes of the commits this entry covers (optional).

human_summary.description: The human-readable wrap-up, written LAST and placed at the very end. A paste-ready release announcement in Markdown -- the actual notes to drop into a release page or CHANGELOG entry. Open with a one-line headline, then short '### Features', '### Fixes', and '### Breaking changes' sections (omit any that are empty) in changelog voice, ending with an upgrade note when there are breaking changes. This restates the categorized entries above as finished prose a reader can publish as-is.
